# #144 - Ränteoron skrämmer techinvesterare, PEG-talets storhet och snigelfart på Parisbörsen!

**Feed**: montrosepodden  
**Published**: 2026-10-15  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Montrose hosts Niklas Andersson and Victor talk about a hot US CPI print, renewed fears of Fed rate hikes before the 28 October decision, and the four-year bull market, which has been carried by AI and is narrowing. Much of the episode explains the PEG and PEGY ratios, using Nvidia and Fortnox as examples of stocks that grew into high P/E multiples. They also cover weak market breadth, OpenAI-driven tech jitters, the slump in French luxury stocks (LVMH, Hermès) amid France's fiscal problems, and Apple's move into home automation.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟡 NVDA — Nvidia | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Both hosts own Nvidia and see AI as the largest tech shift of their lifetime. Earnings growth let the stock grow into its high P/E.

#### Reasoning

The hosts call AI a structural trend and say it is dogmatic to call it a bubble. Victor owns the stock and is glad he does; Niklas bought in 2022 and has not added because the position is already overweight. They expect it to become the first $6tn company. Risks raised: AI growth jitters (OpenAI revenue confusion), circular financing, and memory or Chinese competition pressure.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI revenue growth decelerates materially
- if circular-financing concerns escalate
- if position weight becomes excessive

> *"så äger jag också nu Nvidia sen ett tag tillbaka och det är jag glad över"*

---

### 🟠 AQ — AQ Group | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Called a quality company and success story; Q3 report is due and the hosts visit the company on 21 Oct.

#### Reasoning

The hosts describe the contract manufacturer as a real success story and a quality company. Its largest customer is ABB, the leading Swedish winner from electrification and data centres. Listeners are told to check the upcoming report if interested. There is no explicit buy call, and the Montrose site visit may bias the hosts.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Q3 report disappoints
- if ABB demand weakens

> *"ett kvalitetsbolag måste man ju säga som dessutom har rapport imorgon"*

---

### 🟠 RMS — Hermès | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Down 55% from peak, its largest decline ever, with EV/EBIT 18.9 the lowest in 10+ years. Broad French de-risking may create entry points, but PEG is 2.5.

#### Reasoning

Victor argues that broad thematic rotation away from France can create good entry points in companies that are not doing as badly as the market treats them, and says Hermès is worth a closer look. Niklas counters that PEG 2.5 is high and analysts forecast only modest EPS growth (2.4% in 2026, 10.7% in 2027). Chinese consumer weakness and French fiscal stress remain.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Chinese luxury demand keeps falling
- if French fiscal crisis deepens
- if earnings growth estimates are cut

> *"RMS har evbit 18,9 just nu. Det är lägsta värderingen på över 10 år. Det kanske i alla fall är värt att kika närmare på."*

---

### ⛔ MC — LVMH | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Disappointing report with Fashion & Leather down 5% organically on a weak Chinese consumer. Down 39% YTD, and fund managers plan to cut French exposure.

#### Reasoning

The hosts are negative on near-term momentum: there is no recovery in Chinese consumer demand, LVMH depends heavily on the Chinese middle class, and French sovereign stress is high (10-year yield at 5%, 160bp spread to Germany). Bank of America reports fund managers plan to cut French exposure. They do note that broad sell-offs can create entry points.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Chinese consumer demand rebounds
- if French fiscal situation stabilises

> *"LVMH kom ju med rapport också... Och det var ju också en besvikelse."*

---

### 🟠 ABB — ABB | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Called the winner among engineering companies on electrification and the data-centre boom.

#### Reasoning

The hosts repeatedly call ABB the biggest Swedish winner from the data-centre and electrification boom, and the winner among engineering companies. They give no explicit buy call or valuation view.

#### Sell Triggers

- if data-centre capex slows

> *"Inte bara en vinnare utan verkligen vinnaren bland verkstadsbolagen."*
